This is a tax election, not an award, so no SAM.gov registration or UEI is required. The gross-receipts and five-year tests were not re-verified verbatim against irs.gov in this pass - confirm against the current Form 6765 instructions before relying on them.

eligibility.other_note: Michigan small businesses with fewer than 500 employees (Capital Access Program). Excludes residential housing construction or purchase, casinos, stadiums or arenas and passive real estate. All funding is expected to be repaid.

programmes.source_snippet: The Capital Access Program is an innovative program available to assist businesses with less than 500 employees with capital needs.

programmes.amount_note: Reimbursement-only grants of up to $25,000 per project for new and expanding place-based small businesses (interior renovations, outdoor space, technical assistance, marketing and technology, retail inventory). Paid after project completion via the local applicant organisation. Businesses do not apply directly to MEDC.
programmes.deadline_note: FY26 application window ran March 1 to April 24, 2026 (a correction note says the window closed Monday, April 20 at 5pm). FY26 awards have been announced.
programmes.reopen_note: Contact your local downtown organisation, municipality or Main Street programme ahead of the next annual round.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your local downtown development authority, municipality or Michigan Main Street programme.
The community scores local applications and may submit up to two businesses per round via the MEDC portal.
After project completion, the applicant organisation requests reimbursement.

eligibility.other_note: Place-based small business in a downtown or commercial district of a community designated Essentials or Certified Redevelopment Ready Community, or Select or Master level Michigan Main Street community. Projects must finish within 12 months of grant agreement execution.

programmes.source_snippet: The program provides reimbursement-based grant funding of up to $25,000 per project to support new and expanding place-based small businesses, while leveraging local leadership and community-driven selection.

programmes.funder: Michigan Economic Development Corporation (MEDC), International Trade
programmes.amount_note: Up to $15,000 per fiscal year to offset 75% of pre-approved export expenses: trade missions, international trade shows, foreign sales trips, international marketing media, compliance testing and certifications, sample shipping. Reimbursement on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding.
programmes.deadline_note: FY27 MI-STEP applications are accepted October 15 through September 15, pending funding availability; from October 15, 2026 applications must be submitted at least 10 business days before the activity start date.

procedure_steps.detail: Complete the intake form.
Submit the application at least 10 business days before the trip or activity.
Claim reimbursement with proof of payment after the activity.

documents_required.doc: Michigan LARA annual report or sole proprietorship or partnership filing
EIN linked to a Michigan address
Reimbursement summary worksheet and proof of payment

eligibility.other_note: SBA-size-standard small business organised and operating in the US, in business at least one year, export-ready with at least 51% US content, minimum gross annual revenue of $100,000, EIN linked to a Michigan address, and good standing with the Michigan Department of Treasury. Travel reimbursement limited to two employees who are US citizens.

programmes.source_snippet: Up to $15,000 in assistance is available to offset 75 percent of pre-approved expenses per fiscal year.

programmes.funder: Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity (DCEO)
programmes.amount_note: State match for Illinois companies that hold federal SBIR or STTR awards, with separate Phase I and Phase II application forms. Published award range is $1 to $250,000 with about 55 anticipated awards and $6.5 million estimated total funding. No cost sharing or matching requirement and no indirect costs allowed. Applicants must be GATA pre-qualified.
programmes.deadline_note: Application date range 11/17/2022 to 06/30/2027, 5:00pm.

procedure_steps.detail: Pre-qualify through the Illinois GATA grant system.
Read the NOFO supplement and complete the uniform application.
Submit the Phase I or Phase II match application form.

eligibility.other_note: Illinois-based small business that has received a federal SBIR or STTR Phase I or Phase II award.

programmes.source_snippet: Award Range | $1 - $250,000

programmes.amount_note: Grants for equipment, training, rolling stock, software and facility acquisition or improvements for small businesses in JobsOhio's ten target industries. Grant size is set in the programme guidelines (not stated on the page). Apply through your regional network partner.
programmes.deadline_note: No deadline published; contact your regional network partner.

procedure_steps.detail: Review the JobsOhio Small Business Grant guidelines.
Contact your JobsOhio network partner for your region (Northwest, Northeast, East, West, Central, Southwest, Southeast).

eligibility.other_note: Annual revenues between $100,000 and $25 million; operates within one of JobsOhio's 10 target industries with revenues primarily from B2B sales; at least one year of operating history; planning an eligible investment where the programme's support is instrumental.

programmes.source_snippet: JobsOhio supports small businesses with grants for equipment, training, rolling stock, software, and more—helping you get the resources needed to take the next step.

programmes.name_local: Innovation Ohio Loan Fund (JobsOhio / Ohio Development Services Agency)
programmes.name_en: Innovation Ohio Loan Fund (JobsOhio / Ohio Development Services Agency)
programmes.funder: JobsOhio and the Ohio Development Services Agency
programmes.amount_note: Loans typically $500,000 to $1,500,000, financing up to 75% of allowable project costs (costs capitalisable under GAAP), term 5 to 7 years, fixed rate. Minimum 25% applicant contribution (in-kind not accepted). Fees: 1.75% commitment fee capped at $17,500, 1% annual servicing, 10% participation fee on maximum drawn principal at maturity.
programmes.deadline_note: No deadline published.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact JobsOhio via the Get Started page.
Provide business plan and project details for underwriting.

eligibility.other_note: Existing Ohio company with at least two years of operating history and revenues, a proven product for a proven market, customer orders and prospects for rapid sales growth; committed job creation. Target sectors: advanced materials, instruments/controls/electronics, power and propulsion, biosciences, information technology. Retail projects ineligible.

programmes.source_snippet: The IOF Loan may finance up to 75% of allowable project costs with loans typically ranging in size from $500,000 to $1,500,000.

programmes.funder: JobsOhio and the Ohio Development Services Agency
programmes.amount_note: Capital for expansion projects for companies with limited access to conventional financing: loans typically $500,000 to $1,500,000, terms up to 15 years for real estate and 10 years for machinery and equipment, fixed rate, no prepayment penalty. Requires job creation (typically one job per $35,000 to $75,000 of state loan proceeds) within three years; at least 50% of project costs funded by the borrower and 10% minimum equity.
programmes.deadline_note: No deadline published.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact JobsOhio via the Get Started page.

eligibility.other_note: Projects related to commerce, manufacturing, distribution or research in targeted industries; retail and refinancing ineligible. Commitment fee 1.25% (capped at $12,500) and 0.25% annual servicing fee.

programmes.source_snippet: The program may finance allowable project costs with 166 Direct Loans typically ranging in size from $500,000 to $1,500,000.

programmes.funder: JobsOhio and the Ohio Development Services Agency
programmes.amount_note: Long-term fixed-rate project financing funded by AA+ rated bonds issued by the Ohio Treasurer. Loans typically $2,500,000 to $10,000,000; terms up to 15 years for real estate and 10 years for machinery and equipment; 10% minimum equity contribution and a 10% bond reserve. $30,000 deposit and 2% to 3% closing costs apply.
programmes.deadline_note: No deadline published.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact JobsOhio via the Get Started page.

eligibility.other_note: Developed companies with limited access to funding that create or preserve Ohio jobs (typically one new job per $35,000 to $75,000 of state loan proceeds within three years); retail projects and refinancing ineligible.

programmes.source_snippet: The program may finance allowable project costs with OEBF loans typically ranging in size from $2,500,000 to $10,000,000.

programmes.funder: JobsOhio and the Ohio Tax Credit Authority
programmes.amount_note: Refundable, performance-based tax credit calculated as a percentage of created payroll and applied to the company's commercial activity tax liability; any excess is refunded. Companies must create at least 10 jobs within three years with a minimum annual payroll of $660,000 and pay at least 150% of the federal minimum wage. Approval is by the Ohio Tax Credit Authority.
programmes.deadline_note: No deadline published; approval by the Ohio Tax Credit Authority.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact JobsOhio via the Get Started page.
Final approval by the Ohio Tax Credit Authority.

eligibility.other_note: Ohio companies creating at least 10 jobs within three years with minimum annual payroll of $660,000, paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage.

programmes.source_snippet: Companies creating at least 10 jobs (within three years) with a minimum annual payroll of $660,000 and that pay at least 150 percent of the federal minimum wage are eligible for the credit.

programmes.amount_note: State-funded grants for customised training of new, full-time, permanent employees at new and expanding Florida companies in targeted industries. $7.5 million was allocated for 2025/2026, with priority to first-time applicants. Award size is set in the guidelines (not stated on the page). Has helped more than 950 businesses and over 200,000 employees.
programmes.deadline_note: A notification is posted on the page when funds are no longer available; the 2025/2026 allocation period may have ended, check the page for the current year's allocation.

procedure_steps.detail: Review the QRT guidelines and qualified targeted industries.
Register and apply on the CareerSource Florida applications portal.

documents_required.doc: Sample application information (see CareerSource Florida sample application)

eligibility.other_note: New and expanding Florida businesses in targeted industries creating new full-time, permanent, high-skill jobs.

programmes.source_snippet: Quick Response funds businesses like yours to implement flexible and customized training for your new, full-time, permanent employees.

programmes.amount_note: Reimburses companies for pre-approved training of current full-time employees: up to 50% of direct training costs, and up to 75% for companies with 25 or fewer employees or located in a rural area or county, distressed area, brownfield or HUBZone. Maximum award was $100,000 per company for 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026; each location with a separate FEIN may apply separately.
programmes.deadline_note: No deadline published; the stated maximum applies to the 2025/2026 programme year, so check the page for the current year.

procedure_steps.detail: Review the IWT guidelines.
Apply online via the CareerSource Florida applications portal.

eligibility.other_note: Established Florida businesses training current full-time employees; small businesses are the focus. Training provider chosen by the company.

programmes.source_snippet: The program provides grants for continuing education and training of current full-time employees at Florida companies.

programmes.funder: Technical College System of Georgia (TCSG), Georgia Quick Start
programmes.amount_note: Discretionary incentive providing customised, company-specific workforce training at no cost to companies investing in and creating jobs in Georgia; TCSG states it provides customised training free of charge to qualified new, expanding and existing businesses.
programmes.deadline_note: No deadline published; contact Georgia Quick Start or the Georgia Department of Economic Development.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact Georgia Quick Start through its website or your Georgia Department of Economic Development project manager.

eligibility.other_note: Qualified new, expanding and existing companies investing in and creating jobs in Georgia.

programmes.source_snippet: GEORGIA QUICK START is a discretionary incentive providing CUSTOMIZED, COMPANY-SPECIFIC workforce training at no cost to COMPANIES investing in and CREATING JOBS IN GEORGIA.
